en.text: Article 10 — Dividends. The official Hungarian promulgating act for the Hungary–Czech Republic treaty confirms that the Convention was concluded in English. The treaty provides a 5 per cent source-State ceiling where the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25 per cent of the capital of the payer, and a 15 per cent ceiling in all other cases. The permanent-establishment or fixed-base effective-connection exception applies. This is a concise English synthesis of the official treaty provision; the official treaty controls.

Article 11 — Interest. The official Hungarian promulgating act for the Hungary–Czech Republic treaty confirms that the Convention was concluded in English. Interest arising in one Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State is taxable only in that other State, subject to the permanent-establishment or fixed-base effective-connection exception and the treaty’s arm’s-length limitation. This is a concise English synthesis of the official treaty provision; the official treaty controls.

Article 12 — Royalties. The official Hungarian promulgating act for the Hungary–Czech Republic treaty confirms that the Convention was concluded in English. Royalties beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State may be taxed in the source State subject to a maximum rate of 10 per cent of the gross amount. The permanent-establishment or fixed-base effective-connection exception applies. This is a concise English synthesis of the official treaty provision; the official treaty controls.
